server/cpu-quota.ts.reason: Independent read of this module (not the automated checker) found a second, deeper defect than the prior /tmp/embedding-concurrency-redteam-0809.md review closed: the CPU/memory quota readers only ever checked the cgroup MOUNT ROOT (/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max etc), never this process's own nested cgroup. Verified on this exact sandbox: /proc/self/cgroup places the process five levels below the mount root (/user.slice/.../<scope>.scope), and that leaf's own cgroup.controllers lists only 'memory pids' -- the cpu controller is delegated one level up at app.slice, not down to the leaf, so the leaf has no cpu.max file at all. A systemd/Kubernetes/container-runtime deployment can set a REAL quota at any nested level; a mount-root-only reader silently reads that level's 'no limit configured there' as 'no limit for this process' and over-admits concurrency exactly on the deployment shapes (systemd slices, Kubernetes pods, most container runtimes) where a limit is most likely to actually be set. A follow-up independent review (/tmp/embedding-cgroup-redteam-0810.md) then found and confirmed against primary kernel documentation, plus a live unprivileged nested-systemd-cgroup reproduction on this host, that the FIRST version of this ancestor walk was itself unsound: it returned the NEAREST ancestor's own quota file value, on the false premise that cgroup.subtree_control delegation makes a descendant's declared limit always tighter than or equal to its ancestors'. That premise is wrong -- delegation controls which levels HAVE a quota file, not what numeric value is written into one; the kernel actually enforces the MINIMUM across the whole ancestor chain regardless of which level's file is nearest (Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst; docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-bwc.html). A child scope with its own looser cpu.max than its parent slice is an ordinary, reproducible shape (retightening a parent slice without touching an already-configured child; a Kubernetes namespace-level ResourceQuota above a looser per-pod limit), and reading only the nearest file silently reported that looser (wrong) value. The walk now aggregates EVERY ancestor that has the file and takes the numeric minimum across all 'known' readings ('unlimited' at a level does not participate in the minimum; a malformed reading anywhere in the chain makes the whole aggregate 'unknown', never silently ignored). Also added explicit mountinfo 'root' field (proc(5) field 4) validation: a mount whose root isn't '/' (a bind-mounted cgroup subtree) is now rejected outright rather than relying on the incidental fail-safety of every subsequent read throwing. The +31 mass over the prior 1-point exception (unchanged from the nested-resolution fix, since the aggregation correction and root-field check stayed within the same measured ceiling) is: a minimal correct /proc/self/mountinfo parser (the '-' separator is the only reliable field anchor per proc(5); a fixed-field-count assumption would misparse the variable-length optional-fields section), octal-unescaping for /proc path fields (space/tab/newline/backslash), /proc/self/cgroup parsing for both v2 (hierarchy 0, empty controller list) and v1 (per-named-controller) membership, explicit path-traversal rejection, explicit mountinfo-root-field rejection, and the ancestor-walk-and-aggregate logic itself (collecting every ancestor's own quota reading and reducing to the tightest). Every failure mode (malformed mountinfo/cgroup line, missing separator, ambiguous v1/v2 mapping, ..-traversal, non-'/' mount root, no mount found, a malformed reading anywhere in the aggregated chain) fails closed to 'unknown', never silently falls through to 'unlimited' or to an unaggregated single reading. Proven by test/cpu-quota.test.ts (37 tests): the exact root-unlimited-but-nested-limited case for both CPU and memory on both v1 and v2, tighter-parent/looser-child AND tighter-child/looser-parent in both directions (CPU and memory, v1 and v2), unlimited-child-does-not-mask-a-tighter-parent, a malformed reading anywhere in the chain forcing the whole aggregate to 'unknown', the bind-mounted-subtree root-field rejection, every malformed/traversal/ambiguous-mapping fail-closed path, and two separate mutation-kill checks (recorded during development, not committed) confirming 11 of 28 tests fail if the ancestor walk skips aggregation entirely (mount-root-only) and 7 of 36 fail if the aggregation reduces to first-hit instead of minimum-across-chain.
